entries.title: Distance makes things look better
entries.odia: ଦୂର ପର୍ବତ ସୁନ୍ଦର; ଦୂର ବନ୍ଧୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର
entries.literal_meaning: A distant mountain is beautiful; a distant friend is beautiful.
entries.explanation: Distance can hide the rough edges of a place or a relationship. What looks inviting from afar may feel different when we know its everyday difficulties. The saying gently questions an ideal picture; it does not claim that friendship needs distance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୂରରୁ ଦେଖିଲେ ପାହାଡ଼ର ଅସୁବିଧା ଦିଶେ ନାହିଁ; ଦୂରରେ ଥିବା ବନ୍ଧୁଙ୍କ ଦୋଷ ବି ସହଜରେ ଆଖିରେ ପଡ଼େ ନାହିଁ। ନିକଟରୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅସୁବିଧା ଓ ଦୁର୍ବଳତା ଜଣାପଡ଼େ—ଏହି ତଫାତକୁ କଥାଟି ସୂଚାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Someone envies a friend’s life from holiday photographs; a longer visit reveals ordinary chores and worries too. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary gives two parallel images: a mountain seen from afar and a friend kept at a distance. This explanation is an editorial reading of that contrast, not an origin story.

entries.odia_summary: ଦୂରରୁ ଦେଖିଲେ ପାହାଡ଼ ଓ ବନ୍ଧୁ—ଉଭୟଙ୍କ ଦୁର୍ବଳତା ଲୁଚିଯାଇପାରେ। ନିକଟରୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବଦଳିପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: Distance can hide the rough edges of a place or a friendship. Knowing either closely may change the picture.

entries.title: Giving someone a rough reception
entries.explanation: The ordinary words suggest grades of quality, but together they can describe harsh treatment. In the dictionary’s example, the speaker sends someone away after giving them blows and abuse. The expression conveys that rough reception; reading the words as praise would miss the point. The source records the usage, not a recommendation to treat anyone this way.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଲଗା ଅଲଗା ଭାବେ ‘ଉତ୍ତମ’ ଓ ‘ମଧ୍ୟମ’ ଗୁଣର ମାନ ବୁଝାଏ। କିନ୍ତୁ ଏଠାରେ କାହାକୁ ‘ଉତ୍ତମ ମଧ୍ୟମ ଦେବା’ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରିବା ନୁହେଁ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଉଦାହରଣରେ ଏହା ମାଡ଼ ଓ ଗାଳି ଦେଇ ବିଦା କରିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ। ଏହା କଥାର ଅର୍ଥ ବୁଝାଏ; ସେଭଳି ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: In a fictional account of a quarrel, a neighbour says that a visitor was given “uttama madhyama” before being sent away. The phrase signals a rough encounter, not a warm welcome. This is an original illustrative situation, not a collected account.
entries.cultural_context: This is an idiomatic expression documented within a dictionary example, rather than a complete proverbial sentence. The entry heading uses an editorial infinitive for easy lookup. The witness retains the sentence’s actual inflected wording and the dictionary’s explanation. No claim is made about when or where the expression began.
